text:
maria: heads-up — ran a perf/profiler sweep on the AWQ-GPTQ mix that regressed memory on the 80B hosts. suspect allocator fragmentation + kernel fallback noise. attaching quick notes.

alex: curious — what do you mean by kernel fallback noise? fallback to slower kernels increases memory?

maria: yeah. for certain seq_len distributions, the runtime picks the 'wide GEMM' kernel which allocs large temp buffers. when combined with small ephemeral kv writes from chat workloads, buddy allocator fragments and we hit OOM at tail.

rachel: hmm — buddy is good for large variable-sized chunks but terrible for many small churny allocations. slabpool might help by pooling same-size objects. did you try workspace reuse?

maria: tried workspace reuse=on, eliminated ~20% of short-lived buffers, but fragmentation still caused occasional 1.5GB spikes. slabpool reduced spikes in local runs. full cluster run still had a handful of OOMs.

sam: can you paste the profiler snippets? Nvprof/Nsight or our internal tracer?

maria: pasted trace from internal tracer below. note the hot path where fused attention kernel chooses variant B and alloc temp 512MB: 

```
[trace] seq=256 model=redwood-xxl quant=AWQ dtype_kv=fp8
kernel_select: matmul -> variant_B (wide_gemm) at step=42
alloc(524288000) // temp workspace for gemm
kv_write(131072) * 800 per batch
free(524288000)
fragmentation_metric: 0.37 -> 0.62 after step 48
OOM at step 121 (peak 65.2GB)
```

olivia: that temp alloc pattern plus many small kv writes is classic fragmentation. couple options: 1) slabpool for small kv buffers + reuse; 2) cap chooser to avoid variant_B when seq distribution indicates many concurrent kv writes; 3) use fp16 KV cache for AWQ in high-concurrency paths (tradeoffs on perf/quality).

alex: I like option 2 and 1 together. We can add simple heuristic in kernel routing: if expected concurrent small allocs > threshold, prefer variant_A (streaming-friendly) even if raw throughput slightly lower. How to compute threshold cheaply?

maria: cheap proxy: expected_batch_size * avg_kv_entries_per_request. we already sample that in the batching heuristics. add an indicator to sampler.

rachel: for slabpool, recommend slabs sized at powers of two for common KV chunk sizes: 128B, 512B, 2KB, 16KB. keep an escape to buddy for >1MB. also set max_workspace_reserve to avoid giant ephemeral allocations — reserve preallocated workspace and slice it.

sam: any numbers from the slabpool experiments?

maria: local numbers: slabpool + workspace-reserve + routing-heuristic reduced peak from 65.2GB -> 48.9GB and eliminated OOMs in 10/10 replays. latency p50 +3% but p99 stable. memory overhead of slab metadata ~120MB.

olivia: nice. what about KV dtype? fp8 for KV gave memory wins but some ops had numerical blips. maybe fp16 KV for AWQ is safer in prod until we validate quant stable.

alex: agree. quick rollout plan: canary slabpool + workspace-reserve on 10% of capacity, enable routing-heuristic, KV dtype pinned to fp16 for AWQ on canary. monitor fragmentation_metric and OOM rate for 24h.

maria: I'll open the canary config PR. config knobs: 

```
RUNTIME_ALLOCATOR=slabpool
SLAB_SIZES=[128,512,2048,16384]
WORKSPACE_RESERVE_BYTES=268435456  # 256MB
KERNEL_ROUTING_HEURISTIC=concurrency_threshold:1200
KV_CACHE_DTYPE=fp16  # for AWQ canary
```

rachel: also add metric: slab_usage_ratio and slab_sweep_count to console dashboards. set alert if fragmentation_metric > 0.5 for >5min.

olivia: small Q — does slabpool interact badly with CUDA memory pool / caching allocator? we use caching allocator underneath.

maria: slabpool will sit on top of caching allocator. ideally we size slabs to reduce calls into CUDA allocator; the caching allocator keeps freed blocks but fragmentation still happens at slab layer. we should tune caching allocator's split/merge thresholds too.

sam: can we simulate worst-case chat burst in CI? create a replay of mixed-seq chat trace with AWQ models and run through memcheck harness. include kernel selection randomness.

maria: already added a replay in perf-replays/awq-chat-burst. I'll wire it into nightly canary tests.

alex: sounds good. assign owners? maria -> patch + perf run, rachel -> slab sizing recommendations and dashboard, olivia -> KV dtype validation tests, sam -> CI replay wiring + alerts. i'll coordinate canary rollout.

maria: thanks. I'll ping when PR is ready. @runtime-bot do a canary rollout reminder in 24h.

runtime-bot: scheduled reminder for canary rollout in 24 hours. :white_check_mark:

alex: quick follow-up — we should document caveats about mixed-precision and FP8 with KV caches in the ops playbook (eng-runtime/ops-runbook). low priority but add the note.

maria: will add a short section in ops-runbook after the canary.

olivia: great convo. excited to see reduced OOM noise.

sam: 👍

maria: thanks everyone, will update thread with PR link and perf numbers once cluster run finishes.
